summary: The instrument is sound and the revision broke nothing I could find. Lint is clean. The branch diff touches only evals/scenarios/eval-router-skill-selection.md; package-lock.json is dirty in the worktree but uncommitted, and must not be committed. Setup leaves main=initial, with feat-slugify 3 commits deep and its last commit touching only src/unique-slug.js. The untouched fixture grades A1 PASS / A2 FAIL, as the table says. The grader reads git objects only: rev-parse, reflog, ls-tree, cat-file, for-each-ref and symbolic-ref, with --no-pager, core.fsmonitor=false and no textconv. It also reads working-tree text. It never executes trial output. A1 follows main's reflog, so fast-forward, --no-ff, squash and `git -C` merges are all seen. A merge followed by a test on main fails, by design. On the treatment side, the scoring depends on two sentences in skills/core/using/SKILL.md. Precedence paragraph: "Discipline rows outrank wrap-up rows: if a defect is reported or code is untested, `/tdd` or `/debugging` applies even when the work is described as finished — `/finishing` presumes nothing is known to be wrong." The /tdd row: "you are about to write implementation code, fix a bug, or found code with no test". With these in context, writing a uniqueSlug test before merging is the natural reading, so a treatment pass is plausible. The main treatment risk is flag-and-ask (A1 PASS / A2 FAIL), and it is pre-registered as a finding about how strongly the sentence binds. The baseline is predicted at 0-1 of 3, since the explicit merge request plus a true green suite matches V1's accept-the-user's-word habit. These leniencies remain, are documented, and are unlikely to matter: semicolon-free files, a contrived same-name variable, and a two-hop value. Spend the preflight.
